title: Getting back into some hobby game dev with AI
author: Mindless_Software_99
selftext:
After finding some pixel art tools (pixie.haus majorly) I decided to take a wack at a project that I thought would be cool. I'm good at telling stories and lore I think but just didn't have the visual aptitude to bring a story to life.

I started off with an idea and then used ChatGPT to generate some concept art for a character and naming. I then used ChatGPT to help me create a prompt to plug into [pixie.haus](http://pixie.haus) to create character sprites. I also used ChatGPT to generate some pixel environments. I also used ChatGPT for some of the code (especially the rain effect in the background). 

Animations are also created in pixie.haus. I am using Game Maker Studio for the game engine. So, it's a mix of both manual work and AI work. Let me know your thoughts!

comments.author: Shalke97
comments.body:
This looks really neat! One thing I noticed is that some of the assets look as though they were created at a much higher level of detail and then pixelated afterward. The character and its animations especially give that impression.

If you’re aiming for this kind of pixel-art style, I’d recommend using fewer but more prominent details instead of trying to preserve a realistic look. At the moment, some parts appear a little mushy as a result.

The talking head looks great, though! I did notice a few white pixels on the left side of the hair, where the background should probably be transparent. You may want to clean up those frames afterward.

Other than that, I wish you the best of luck with the project!

replies.author: Mindless_Software_99
replies.body:
Thank you for pointing that out! I realized that and decided to make some adjustments to the background to make the pixeallation more consistent.

 I'm definitely excited to see where it goes!

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: Ghost Trick is a good example of this downscaling to pixel art. It has some of the best pixel art animation I've ever seen, two decades later. Note: not talking about the vector art remaster.

comments.author: StworowskiGamedev
comments.body: Overall, the style looks very cool and very cool concept, but for me it still looks a bit too AI-generated. First, the pixel art isn’t very precise, some pixels appear to be placed randomly, which doesn’t look intentional. I used [PixelLab.ai](http://PixelLab.ai) and I remember it had an option for technically refining pixel art. Also, I notice a lot of noise and grime on the objects. AI tends to add these artifacts quite heavily, so you have to work hard on the prompt to prevent them from appearing.

comments.author: Lumpz1
comments.body: Looks cool! If you have the talking head marking who is the speaker of a text box, you probably don’t also need “Me:” marking the speaker as well, imo
